facts.statement: The genus Fissuravis was named by Mayr in 2007.
Fossils of Fissuravis date to the Selandian stage of the Paleocene epoch.
Fissuravis is an extinct bird genus found in Paleocene deposits in Germany.
facts.quote: Fissuravis ("fissure bird") is a genus of extinct bird from the Paleocene of Germany.

facts.statement: Fissuravis belongs to the family Lithornithidae and is closely related to modern ratites.
facts.quote: A lithornithid, it was closely related to modern ratites, but it was a capable flyer.

facts.statement: Unlike its relatives, Fissuravis was a capable flyer.
facts.quote: A lithornithid, it was closely related to modern ratites, but it was a capable flyer.

facts.statement: Fossils of Fissuravis come from the Walbeck Paleocene deposits.
facts.quote: Hailing from the Walbeck Paleocene deposits, it is found amidst a rich avian fauna, which also included the gigantic Gastornis and the enigmatic ratite Remiornis.

facts.statement: Remnants of the coracoid suggest Fissuravis had powerful flight muscles and likely engaged in soaring flight.
facts.quote: Like most lithornithids, it was probably a very competent flyer, its coracoid remnants suggesting powerful flight musculature, and it likely engaged in a similar style of soaring flight to Lithornis and Pseudocrypturus.

facts.statement: Fissuravis is classified within the parent group Lithornithidae.
The type species of the genus Fissuravis is Fissuravis weigelti.
Fissuravis lived between 61.66 and 59.24 million years ago during the Selandian.
facts.quote: Time range: Selandian to Selandian (61.66 to 59.24 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Fissuravis is classified in the class Aves.
